tip: Someone else's wish normally takes -고 싶어해요: 되고 싶어해요 (doego sipeohaeyo = wants to become).
못 (mot) + verb = 'cannot / didn't manage': 못 했어요 (motaesseoyo = couldn't do).
께서 (kkeseo) replaces 이/가 (i/ga) when the subject deserves respect, and the verb takes -세요 (-seyo) to match: 아버지께서 보세요 (abeojikkeseo boseyo = father watches).
Interest is an amount in Korean: 관심이 많아요 (gwansimi manayo) = literally 'interest is a lot', not 'I am interested'.
만 (man = only) follows the noun: 기사만 (gisaman = only articles).
-(으)면 (-(eu)myeon) covers 'whenever', not just 'if': 읽으면 (ilgeumyeon) = when(ever) I read them.
넘다 (neomda = to exceed) takes 이/가: 백 명이 넘어요 (baengmyeongi neomeoyo = over 100).
안 (an) in front of the verb makes it negative: 안 올려요 (an ollyeoyo = don't post).
개 (gae) counts things, normally with native numbers: 두 개 (du gae = two).
(으)로 marks a change-into: 비공개로 (bigonggaero = into private).
구독하다 (gudokada = to subscribe) takes 을/를: 채널을 구독했어요 (chaeneoreul gudokaesseoyo = subscribed to the channel).
편 (pyeon) counts films, normally with native numbers: 세 편 (se pyeon = three films).
개 (gae) is the all-purpose counter for things, and low counts use native numbers: 다섯 개 (daseot gae) = five (seasons) – Sino 오 개 (o gae) would be wrong here.
-(으)면 = 'when': 나오면 (naomyeon = when it comes out).
의 (pronounced e here) shows possession: 가수의 영상 (gasu-e yeongsang = the singer's video).
(으)로 marks the tool: 유튜브로 (yutyubeuro = via YouTube).
-(으)면서 = 'while': 보면서 (bomyeonseo = while watching).
-(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can': 볼 수 있어요 (bol su isseoyo = can view).
(으)로 marks the result: 드라마로 (deuramaro = into a drama).
-(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 여행할 때 (yeohaenghal ttae = when traveling).
시 uses native numbers: 여섯 시 (yeoseot si = six o'clock).
다 되다 = 'be all used up': 다 됐어요 (da dwaesseoyo = is dead/empty).
-고 오다 = 'do and come': 두고 왔어요 (dugo wasseoyo = left it and came).
번 (beon = times) normally uses native numbers: 스무 번 (seumu beon = twenty times).
(으)로 marks the cause here: 실수로 (silsuro = by mistake).
Respectful form of a feeling someone else has: 어려워하세요 (eoryeowohaseyo = they find it hard).
-도 (-do = even/also): 해외에서도 (haeoeseodo = even abroad).
덕분에 (deokbune = thanks to) follows a noun: 앱 덕분에 (aep deokbune = thanks to the app).
점 (jeom = points) uses Sino numbers: 오 점 (o jeom = five points).
이다 (ida = to be) turns into -라서 for 'because it is': 무료라서 (muryoraseo = because it's free).
